newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal, ton-miles strong in Q1 - AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal, ton-miles strong in Q1 - AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail intermodal freight and ton-miles were strong in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period in 1996, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
In the first 13 weeks of 1997, AAR said intermodal traffic rose 5.4 percent to 2.06 million trailers and containers from 1.96 million in the same 1996 period. Intermodal does not include carloads.

Ton-miles were up four percent in the first quarter to 348.2 billion from 334.7 billion in year-ago quarter, AAR said. Carloads also rose 3.3 percent to 4.36 million from 4.22 million from the year-ago period.
"Both intermodal and ton-miles set records for the first quarter," Craig Rockey, AAR senior assistant vice president, said.
But Rockey added, "weather wasn't as much of a factor in the eastern U.S. this year as it was during last year's first quarter."

AAR said intermodal freight rose 5.9 percent in the week ended March 29 to 169,516 trailers and containers from 160,085 in the year-ago week. Ton-miles rose 1.1 percent to 27.4 billion in the week from 27.1 billion last year. The ton-mile equates one ton of freight hauled one mile.
Carloads in the March 29 week rose 0.5 percent to 343,860 from 342,299 in the year-ago week.

AAR said there were significant increases in carloads of coke, up 14 percent to 5,630 carloads in the week from 4,939 a year ago, while metals and related products increased 9.5 percent to 14,042 carloads from 12,828.

Coal loadings totaled 138,084, up 5.6 percent from 130,794 a year ago, while grain mill products increased 3.5 percent to 9,477 carloads from 9,156. Motor vehicles and parts rose 2.6 percent in the week to 20,557 carloads from 20,042 last year.

But AAR said there were sharp decreases in loadings of grain, down 16.6 percent in the March 29 week to 23,235 carloads from 27,867 in the same 1996 week. Metallic ores fell 14.1 percent to 14,738 carloads from 17,155 last year, while nonmetallic minerals totaled 8,202 carloads, a 9.2 percent decline from 9,030.

AAR also said carloads on Canada's two transcontinental railroads totaled 52,950 in the March 29 week, a 2.2 percent drop from a year ago, but intermodal traffic rose 2.3 percent to 24,137 trailers and containers from the same 1996 week.

In the first 13 weeks of 1997, AAR said U.S. carloads on the Canada railroads totaled 5.03 million, up 2.9 percent from the same 1996 period, while intermodal traffic rose 5.8 percent to 2.37 million trailers and containers from the year-ago period.
